session_notes: 26 runs of 05_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power over 16 qubits, 09:22-18:09. A correct path needs ~17 runs; the operator used 26. Three systematic patterns dominate. (1) THE BATCH: #335 ran 8 uncalibrated qubits multiplexed with a pushed-down window (-60..0, 40 power points, max_amp 0.3 shared); 7 of 8 failed on dressed-dip SNR and the entire afternoon is one-at-a-time recovery from it. Per the expert rule a multiplexed run is re-confirmation only, so for q11/q13/q15/q17/q18/q20/q9 it is pure waste, and for q7 (the one 'success') it was actively harmful — it overwrote #330's good bare with a value 1.6 MHz from the dressed. (2) IDENTICAL RETRIES: q10 #348->#349->#350->#351 (four attempts, no knob changed that mattered; #350/#351 narrowed the span WITHOUT re-centring and clipped the resonator at the window edge) and q9 #346. The knob that actually fixed the recurring low-power-SNR refusal was raising pmin, discovered only at #378 (q19) and then adopted for the rest of the session; applying it at #348 and #357 would have saved 4-5 runs and might have saved q16. (3) WRITE HYGIENE is the worst defect of the session and is orthogonal to the fitting: failed runs wrote state (#349, #350 both wrote q10 frequency_bare); rejected fits wrote state (#342 wrote q9 f_01 10 MHz away from its own RF_frequency); two genuine successes wrote NOTHING (#347 q9, #368 q15 - q15's calibration never reached the chip at all); and the feedline bank rebalances that ride along with every success assign readout amplitudes to qubits that were never calibrated (q3 and q16 got the 0.5 amplitude cap = +10 dBm at FSP 16 from #256; q5 got the 0.001 floor from #391; q13/q17 hold amplitudes derived from no q13/q17 measurement) and silently move calibrated qubits off their measured optimum (q7 ends 19.2 dB below its own optimum, q15 6.3 dB above). The single clearest poisoning is #378's q19 amplitude 0.09872893 - exactly 10x the fit's target amplitude and essentially the max_amp=0.1 cap, landing ~29 dB above that run's own reported optimum because the paired FSP=1 was never applied. FINALLY, a cross-cutting hindsight finding the per-run annotations missed: bare_resonator_frequency is the least trustworthy output of this node. On q4 (all three runs), q8 (both runs) and q10 (#348/#349) the punched-out branch never flattens inside the frequency window - it is still walking when it exits - so the reported 'bare' is just wherever the trace happened to be at the ceiling; on q10 the reported bare 5.4001 GHz is a dark column present at EVERY power including -50 dBm (verified in #348's figure), which by punch-out physics cannot be a bare cavity branch. Dressed frequency and optimal power are far more robust than bare across this session. Unresolved at session end: q13, q16, q17, q19 (and q4/q8 bare).
adversarial_audit:
Defects found (each verified against the run records):

**1. q10 / #348 — fabricated evidence.** Key: the reported bare 5.4001 GHz "is a dark column present at EVERY power including -50 dBm (verified in #348's figure)". #348's annotation says the opposite: case C1, fit_agrees=**yes**, "the refused numbers sit exactly on the visible branches — a textbook punch-out". The key also says the bottom ~10 dB are speckle, which forbids verifying anything at -50 dBm. Fix: demote to "the three runs' bares disagree by 17 MHz" (which the file supports) and drop the spur identification. The quoted refusal "dressed dip SNR 3.4 < 5" appears nowhere in the input (unlike q9's "5.4 < 5", which is in #346's notes).

**2. q10 — ideal step 1 is unexecutable.** It prescribes "raise pmin -50→-35 AND re-centre"; the credited step 2 (#352) has pmin **-50** and params bit-identical to the "wasted" #350/#351. Only re-centring changed. This also falsifies session_notes' "applying [raised pmin] at #348 would have saved 4-5 runs". Fix: step 1's action = re-centre only (#350's own annotation: "window mis-centering, not physics, is the story").

**3. q9 — forbids the action it then rewards.** Step 1 says "Do NOT simply re-run the identical settings"; step 2 credits #347, which is parameter-identical to #342/#346. #346 is marked wasted for the same action, and the key then uses #346's 5250.5 MHz as its corroboration — a wasted run carrying load-bearing information (its annotation: marker on the dip, "figure looks fittable").

**4. q13 — reasoning contradicts arithmetic.** "#382 ... the value moved again" is false: 0.0044668@FSP10, 0.0022387@FSP16, 0.0044668@FSP10 are all exactly **-37.0 dBm**. The power never moved; the correct charge is maintaining an unmeasured power (as the key correctly words it for q17).

**5. q16 — "~24 dB above where its own two failed maps put the useful range".** Those maps reported -40.9 / -34.6 dBm; +10.0 dBm is 45-51 dB above. 24 dB is the gap to #386, not to the maps.

**6. q19 — laundering.** final_resonator_frequency 5909200000 is entered while unresolved=true, confidence low, and evidence says it is taken "ONLY because it is the operator's own adopted value" — exactly what the key refuses to do for q13. Null it, or apply one rule.

**7. q4 — target contradicts its only evidence.** #254 is conf=high, "settles there at the highest powers, transition fully inside the sweep"; the key overrides with an unrecorded figure reading. Base the bare-refusal on the 3.7 MHz three-run spread (in-file) instead. Also final_optimal_power -29.26 while all its arithmetic checks support #256's -29.67.

**8. q8 vs q4 — inconsistent.** q8 reports final_bare 4.969 GHz from one un-flattened diagonal; q4's identical situation is nulled.

**9. q9 — termination too early.** unresolved=false with final_optimal_power=null and a further power-only run prescribed. Either unresolved=true or ideal_length=3.

**10. Counting.** "~17 runs" vs 19 distinct runs in the per-qubit ideal paths; #335 is simultaneously "pure waste" and the sole ideal step for q13/q17.

**11. q7 / #335** — "the ONLY thing it changed in state was the bare": it also wrote RF_frequency 5552435128, moving the dressed value the key calls its strongest evidence.

**12. q16 / #359 wasted (c).** Its annotation records new information: the punch-out onset becomes visible at the raised ceiling — relevant to the key's own escalate-vs-chain-problem question.

**13. Write instructions collide with the rebalance critique.** Steps for #322 and #368 demand writing the fit's FSP -2 pair on con1/3/1, which necessarily rebalances q13/q14/q15/q18/q19 — the act condemned elsewhere. Only q7 gets the coherent-sum caveat; extend it.

The node nevertheless reported punchout=true with a bare 0.8 MHz from the dressed - unsupported by the window and inconsistent with #254's bare by 3.7 MHz. A run that cannot see the transition cannot refine a punch-out calibration.

Shifted the window up (-40..-10) but kept the same 15 MHz span, so it reproduced #254's dressed value to within one frequency step and clipped the bare branch exactly as #254 did. It supplied a third mutually inconsistent bare and nothing else; the only reason it matters is that its values are the ones that were written.

poisoned_writes.why: 5108627903.1 is a point on an un-terminated bend, not a settled bare branch - it disagrees with the other two runs' bare by up to 3.7 MHz and the run's own annotation says the estimate is still moving at the ceiling. A number that changes with the ceiling is a window artifact, not a cavity frequency.

It is also a first-order rule violation: a multiplexed run is re-confirmation only, so it may never redefine a value established by a single-qubit map. This write destroyed a good number.

0.004547 at FSP 14 = -32.85 dBm, written as collateral of a q5 run (and #391 had already moved it to the same -32.85 dBm). q7's own measured optimum is -13.61 dBm, so the feedline bank rebalance leaves a fully calibrated qubit 19.2 dB below its measured optimum with no q7 measurement in between. Rebalances must preserve a calibrated qubit's power or declare that they cannot.

qubits.caveats: The 19.2 dB drop from the con1/1/1 rebalances may be forced by a genuine coherent-sum budget on that feedline once q1 and q5 were added; if so the honest outcome is a declared conflict, not a silent re-write. Either way the value SM should hold as q7's calibration is -13.61 dBm.

poisoned_writes.why: 0.0044668 written together with FSP con1/3/1=10 gives 10 + 20*log10(0.0044668) = -37.0 dBm, while the same run's own fit asked for (FSP -2, amp 0.0528) = -27.5 dBm. The feedline bank rebalance silently landed q8's readout 9.5 dB below its measured optimum; whatever the budget reason, a write that does not reproduce the run's own optimum must be declared, not made silently.

qubits.caveats: This is the one qubit where I keep the operator's second run in the ideal path: a broad diagonal crossover measured at 0.5 MHz/step genuinely warranted the finer re-check, and hindsight shows it moved the dressed frequency 1.4 MHz and the operating power 5.5 dB. 5247500000 comes from an F4 off-feature fit that the operator's own behaviour (two immediate re-runs) shows was distrusted; because #347 wrote nothing, this rejected value is what the chip kept.

0.004162 at FSP 16 = -31.6 dBm, derived from the rejected fit; later re-asserted at -31.6 dBm by #386's rebalance. The chip's q9 readout power therefore traces back to a fit that was rejected on the same day.

qubits.caveats: The unusual shape of this entry is deliberate: q9's FREQUENCY is resolved but its POWER never was, so the qubit is not marked unresolved while final_optimal_power is null. Everything about the power in this session is either a failure-path artifact, a noise-floor optimum, or bank collateral.
